evidence.note: Continuous net-count tracking with explicit deltas ('40 passed up from 32', '58 passing 5 failures left'), establishing a running ledger early.
Distinguishes a genuinely-solved pass from a coincidental one — questions why alignment tests passed and checks golden values (EC=0.689 not 0) rather than trusting the green.
Whole-suite re-runs producing per-group counts (51 CLI, 13 lib, 58 analysis, 160/388 total) — maintains an accurate live picture across the large test surface.

Categorizes remaining failures by group (BIF, specialized layouts, link-grouping, roundtrip) and deliberately defers stubborn ones ('skip these for now', 'give up on BIF... don't regress') instead of looping.

Abandons drainZone/BIF as 'far too complex' then later returns with a productive angle (color brighten/darken), showing tactic-change rather than pure thrashing; counts jump 60->77 confirming the ledger.
At the end the suite hangs; agent loses clean live accounting and waits blindly across many turns, though it retains its last-known state (85 parity / ~209 total).

reasoning: The agent maintains an explicit, continuously-updated ledger of pass counts with 'up from X' deltas, categorizes remaining failures per test group, re-runs the whole suite to confirm progress, and even distinguishes coincidental passes from genuine ones (step 61-62) — squarely matching the level-8 anchor and touching level-10 traits (deliberate deferral of stubborn diffs, coincidence detection). It falls short of a 10 because the failure set improved near-monotonically so it never had to catch a regression of a green case, and it lost clean live accounting during the terminal test-hang (steps 271-292). Net behavior sits solidly at 8.
